_strings.@@1a24d67a1c75: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW for 2025 — a 100% CAPITAL GAIN SUBTRACTION on Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 18: "The state of Missouri allows a subtraction from your federal adjusted gross income for 100 percent of your federally reported capital gains. Enter the amount of capital gains reported on your Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, Line 7a" (enter $0 if Line 7a is negative). Total Form MO-A Part 1 subtractions moved from 2024's Line 18 to 2025's Line 19, and Form MO-1040 Line 4 now carries MO-A Part 1 Line 19. A 2025 Missouri taxable income computed without this subtraction will be OVERSTATED. _strings.@@1a6eec29172c: Property Tax Credit Claim (Circuit Breaker) — Missouri residents who fall into one of four qualification categories (2025 Form MO-PTS): (A) 65 years of age or older and a full-year MO resident (attach Form SSA-1099); (B) 100% disabled veteran as a result of military service (attach a letter from the Department of Veterans Affairs); (C) 100% disabled (attach an SSA letter or Form SSA-1099); or (D) 60 years of age or older and received surviving spouse benefits (attach Form SSA-1099). Available to both renters/part-year owners and full-year homeowners. Renters who rent from a facility that does not pay property tax are not eligible.

_strings.@@4393666145eb: Treaty conformity — MO conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MO income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MO return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Missouri's resident return starts from federal adjusted gross income and has no treaty-exempt income add-back, so federally treaty-exempt income (already excluded from federal AGI) flows through untaxed -> conforms. Form MO-1040 Line 1 is captioned "Federal adjusted gross income from federal return," and the 2025 MO-1040 instructions state "You must begin your Missouri return with your total federal adjusted gross income, even if you have income from a state other than Missouri." The only additions to federal AGI are on Form MO-A, Part 1, Lines 1-6 (interest on state and local obligations other than Missouri source; partnership/fiduciary/S-corp adjustments; nonqualified 529-plan distributions; Food Pantry contributions included on federal Schedule A; nonresident property tax modification; nonqualified ABLE-program distributions) — none of which add back federally treaty-exempt income or foreign-earned income. Corroborating: the 2025 "Nonresident Alien Special Filing Instructions" direct the filer to "Enter your federal adjusted gross income from U.S. Nonresident Alien Income Tax Return (Federal Form 1040NR), Line 11a, on Form MO-1040, Line 1," meaning treaty-exempt income already excluded from 1040NR AGI carries to MO Line 1 unchanged with no reattachment. Unlike California (which adds treaty income back on Schedule CA), Missouri has no analogous addback. Cite: 2025 MO-1040 Instructions, Line 1 and Form MO-A Part 1.

_strings.@@6934d69f0c8b: Food Pantry / Homeless Shelter / Soup Kitchen Tax Credit — Any taxpayer (individual, corporation, or trust) who donates cash or food supplies to a local food pantry, homeless shelter, or soup kitchen in the county where the taxpayer resides. If the donation is also reported as a federal Schedule A charitable contribution, the amount must be added back on Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 4 (2025 MO-A Line 4, 'Food Pantry contributions included on Federal Schedule A'). Program sunsets December 31, 2026 (fully terminates September 1, 2027), so tax year 2025 is still within the program.

_strings.@@a13a158c21d3: Missouri Working Family Tax Credit (state EITC) — Resident individual who was allowed a federal earned income credit (EIC) on the federal return for the same tax year; filing status must be single, head of household, qualifying widow(er), or married filing combined (married filing separately does not qualify); must have a tax liability after the application of all other credits. Form MO-WFTC and a copy of the federal return must be attached or the credit may be disallowed.

calls.work_head: MO state income tax (2025, graduated brackets): taxable_base $40,000.00 — which must be the state form's OWN taxable-income line, with the state's deductions/exemptions already computed on the form (this state's deduction is income-dependent or otherwise not a fixed amount the op could subtract) — with no exemptions or standard deduction to subtract; graduated tax on $40,000 [married_filing_jointly (qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column) schedule]: 0 x $1,313.00 (the $0-$1,313 bracket) = $0.00; 0.02 x $1,313.00 (the $1,313-$2,626 bracket) = $26.26; 0.025 x $1,313.00 (the $2,626-$3,939 bracket) = $32.82; 0.03 x $1,313.00 (the $3,939-$5,252 bracket) = $39.39; 0.035 x $1,313.00 (the $5,252-$6,565 bracket) = $45.96; 0.04 x $1,313.00 (the $6,565-$7,878 bracket) = $52.52; 0.045 x $1,313.00 (the $7,878-$9,191 bracket) = $59.08; 0.047 x $30,809.00 (the $9,191+ bracket) = $1,448.02; total $1,704.06 -> $1,704

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form MO-1040 Line 30: 'Tax (see tax chart on page 21 of the instructions)', computed per column (30Y/30S) from Line 29Y/29S. Instructions p.21, '2025 Tax Chart': 'To identify your tax, use your Missouri taxable income from Form MO-1040, Line 29Y and 29S and the tax chart in Section A below. A separate tax must be computed for you and your spouse. Calculate your Missouri tax using the online tax calculator at dor.mo.gov/personal/individual/ or by using the worksheet in Section B below. Round to the nearest whole dollar and enter on Form MO-1040, Line 30Y and 30S.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 CHANGES: the top rate fell AGAIN, to 4.7% (2024: 4.8%; 2023: 4.95%), and the chart's income steps re-indexed to $1,313 increments (2024: $1,273) — breakpoints $1,313 / $2,626 / $3,939 / $5,252 / $6,565 / $7,878 / $9,191, with the printed constants $26 / $59 / $98 / $144 / $197 / $256. Verified against BOTH the 2025 MO-1040 instructions p.21 and the 2025 MO-1040A short-form instructions (identical chart), and corroborated a third time by the booklet's composite-return note 'The tax rate for a composite return is 4.7 percent.' 2025 BASE CHANGE — NEW 100% CAPITAL GAIN SUBTRACTION (affects the taxable_base you must supply): Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 18 is new for 2025 — 'The state of Missouri allows a subtraction from your federal adjusted gross income for 100 percent of your federally reported capital gains. Enter the amount of capital gains reported on your Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, Line 7a' (if Line 7a is negative, enter $0). Total subtractions moved from 2024's MO-A Part 1 Line 18 to 2025's Line 19, and Form MO-1040 Line 4 now carries MO-A Part 1 Line 19. A 2025 Missouri taxable income computed without this subtraction will be OVERSTATED. Base guidance: Supply 2025 Form MO-1040 Line 29 'Taxable income' — one column at a time: Line 29Y (yourself) or Line 29S (spouse). Line 29 = total Missouri AGI (Line 6, which starts from federal AGI at Line 1 plus Form MO-A Part 1 additions at Line 2 and minus Form MO-A Part 1 total subtractions at Line 4, now MO-A Line 19 including the new 100% capital gain subtraction) minus total deductions (Line 25 = Line 8 plus Lines 13 through 24: the pension/Social Security exemption; the Lines 9-13 FEDERAL INCOME TAX DEDUCTION — Line 11 federal tax x a percentage set by Missouri AGI: 35% if Line 6 is $25,000 or less, 25% for $25,001-$50,000, 15% for $50,001-$100,000, 5% for $100,001-$125,000, 0% for $125,001 or more, capped at $5,000 per individual / $10,000 married filing combined; the Line 14 standard or itemized deduction; the Line 15 $1,400 head-of-household/qualifying-widow(er) exemption; and the other deductions on Lines 16-24, with Lines 20, 22, and 23 'Reserved' for 2025), giving Line 26; then apportioned by each spouse's income percentage (Line 7Y/7S, applied at Line 27), minus any Line 28 enterprise-zone/rural-empowerment modification = Line 29. Single, married filing separately, head of household, and qualifying widow(er) filers have one column — supply that Line 29 amount. MARRIED FILING COMBINED: Missouri taxes each spouse's column separately — run this op once with Line 29Y and once with Line 29S and add the two results (Form MO-1040 Lines 30Y + 30S); do NOT supply the couple's combined taxable income as one amount, or the tax will be overstated. One rate schedule for all filing statuses: the 2025 Tax Rate Chart (MO-1040 instructions p.21) makes no distinction by filing status, so the identical schedule is shipped for all four statuses. Qualifying widow(er) maps to married_filing_jointly here and uses the same chart. CRITICAL for married filing combined: Missouri computes tax SEPARATELY for each spouse — 'A separate tax must be computed for you and your spouse' (instructions p.21). Combined income is split by each spouse's income percentage (Line 7Y/7S, applied at Line 27), producing Line 29Y and 29S, each run through the chart (Line 30Y/30S), then added at Line 36. Running a couple's combined taxable income through the brackets as one amount OVERSTATES tax (a second pass through the below-4.7% brackets). Run this op once per spouse's Line 29 column and sum the results. Printed-constant rounding (quantified for 2025): the chart's flat add-on constants ($26 / $59 / $98 / $144 / $197 / $256) are rounded from the exact cumulative marginal sums ($26.26 / $59.085 / $98.475 / $144.43 / $196.95 / $256.035); the largest divergence is $0.475 at the $5,252 breakpoint. This op does exact marginal math, so its result can differ from the form worksheet's result by up to ~$1 after rounding. Both agree on the booklet's own worked examples (Example A, taxable income $3,090: worksheet 26 + 11.60 = 37.60 -> 38, exact marginal 26.26 + 11.60 = 37.86 -> 38; Example B, $12,000: worksheet 256 + 132.03 = 388.03 -> 388, exact marginal 256.035 + 132.023 = 388.058 -> 388). Where they can split is a top-bracket amount whose exact total lands on a .50 tie (exact = printed + $0.035 there), e.g. taxable income $9,286: exact 260.50 -> 261 while the worksheet's 256 + 4.465 = 260.465 -> 260. The filed return should use the p.21 Tax Calculation Worksheet's printed constants or the DOR online calculator at dor.mo.gov/personal/individual/. Federal income tax deduction (Missouri base quirk, NOT modeled): MO-1040 Lines 9-13 deduct Line 11 federal income tax times a Missouri-AGI-based percentage (Line 12 chart: 35% if Line 6 is $25,000 or less; 25% $25,001-$50,000; 15% $50,001-$100,000; 5% $100,001-$125,000; 0% $125,001 or more), capped at $5,000 per individual / $10,000 married filing combined. Because it is income-dependent it is not modeled — it must already be reflected in the Line 29 taxable income you supply. standard_deduction ships as null because the base is Line 29 taxable income, from which the Line 14 deduction was already subtracted — do not subtract it again. For reference, 2025 Missouri standard deductions (printed on Form MO-1040 Line 14): $15,750 single or married filing separate; $23,625 head of household; $31,500 married filing combined or qualifying widow(er). Additional standard deduction for each 65-or-older or blind condition (Line 14 instructions, CHANGED for 2025): $2,000 for single and head of household (2024: $1,950); $1,600 for married filing combined, married filing separately, or qualifying widow(er) (2024: $1,550). A net qualified disaster loss increase to the federal standard deduction increases the Missouri one by the same amount (paper filing required). Itemizers use Form MO-A Part 2 instead — the 2025 MO-A prints its Part 2 worksheet trigger as "Complete this worksheet only if your total state and local taxes included in your federal itemized deductions exceeded $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately) or you were required to complete a federal worksheet to calculate Federal Schedule A, Line 5e." (no AGI figure of its own). Head of household / qualifying widow(er) additional exemption: $1,400 on MO-1040 Line 15 (unchanged for 2025) — a base reduction already included in the Line 29 base, so it is not shipped; the Missouri filing status must match the federal filing status to claim it. The 2025 MO-1040 has NO personal or dependent exemption lines — exemptions is intentionally empty; exemptions_count and dependents_count have no effect for Missouri. Zero-rate floor: Missouri taxable income of $0 to $1,313 owes $0 (shipped as a rate-'0' bottom bracket); the state is graduated, not flat, for 2025. Rounding rule (instructions 'Dollars and Cents': 'For 1 cent through 49 cents, round down to the previous whole dollar amount. For 50 cents through 99 cents, round up to the next whole dollar amount', with the booklet's own examples 'Round $32.49 down to $32.00' and 'Round $32.50 up to $33.00') — matches the engine's half-up rounding, and vector 1 below is the exact .50 half-up tie. No lookup-table mandate: Missouri publishes no tax table; all filers compute Line 30 from the Tax Rate Chart / Tax Calculation Worksheet (Section B) or the DOR online calculator. Not modeled — MO-1040 Line 34 other taxes: tax on lump-sum distributions (10% of the tax shown on Federal Form 4972) and recapture of low income housing credits (Federal Form 8611); these are added after Line 30 on the form. Not modeled — apportionment and credits after Line 30: nonresidents/part-year residents multiply Line 30 by the Missouri income percentage (Line 32, Form MO-NRI), and residents may take the resident credit for taxes paid to other states (Line 31, Form MO-CR); this op produces the pre-apportionment Line 30 amount. Also not modeled (they are CREDITS against tax, not base reductions): Property Tax Credit (Line 43; Form MO-PTS), Missouri Working Family Tax Credit (Line 44, Form MO-WFTC — still 20% of the federal EIC; the 2025 form's question 3, "Do you have investment income greater than $4,400 (see instructions)?", stops a filer who answers Yes), and miscellaneous credits (Line 42; Form MO-TC). The 2024 MO-1040 printed the same line numbers (42 MO-TC, 43 MO-PTS, 44 MO-WFTC). This pack follows the 2025 Form MO-1040 long form; the MO-1040A short form uses the same 2025 Tax Chart (its instructions were the second-pass source) but has its own line layout.
